summary: This bash function summarizes documents by extracting their text content and sending it to a local AI model with instructions to produce a specific number of bullet points. It supports various file formats through a conversion utility and defaults to 5 bullet points if none are specified.

explanations.9: The ${2:-5} syntax means 'use the second argument if provided, otherwise default to 5' — it's a way to set a fallback value.
explanations.11: This checks that the file argument exists and is actually a file; -z tests if the string is empty, and ! -f tests if the path isn't a regular file.
explanations.17: This calls a helper function to extract plain text from the file (handling PDFs, Word docs, etc.), and the || return 1 means 'if extraction fails, exit this function immediately with an error'.
explanations.19: The variable is being built across multiple lines using a here-doc style — the prompt string contains the instruction text plus a placeholder for the point count, and will include the extracted text below it.
